Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 3 \\u00B7 f959a9a1]\\n\\n- **What exists now.** The branch has four commits on top of \\u006006de56f\\u0060: the claim rules in \\u0060Coanda.Core/Parcels/ClaimDecider.cs\\u0060, the feed gating, then the claim command, held tracking, lost-claim stop and trigger and service gating together, then design doc sections 6, 7 and 14.4. The gates are green after rebasing onto \\u0060origin/main\\u0060.\\n- **Gotchas.**\\n  - Holding is read from the store alone. A claim counts as held when its line\\u0027s sequence is at or below the \\u0060LedgerProgress\\u0060 \\u0022fetched-after-push\\u0022 record. That record moves forward only after a fetch from every clone succeeds, its lines are imported, and a root key record exists. Tests with peers present must call \\u0060TrustRootAsync\\u0060 first.\\n  - Whether an event is this node\\u0027s own is judged by comparing its line\\u0027s origin with the \\u0060LedgerOrigin\\u0060 document, not with \\u0060NodeIdentity\\u0060. A test that fakes this node\\u0027s own lines must store \\u0060LedgerOrigin\\u0060 too.\\n  - \\u0060LostClaims\\u0060 stops losing flow runs at the end of each import round as the \\u0060coanda-claims\\u0060 Agent principal, through \\u0060flow-run.yield\\u0060.\\n- **Left undone on purpose.** These are the brief\\u0027s non-goals:\\n  - leases, and releasing or transferring a claim;\\n  - the winner restarting a binding after the loser\\u0027s flow run releases the parcel (decision 2d0ab2d3);\\n  - gating feed kinds other than flow run ended and stopped;\\n  - deciding which roles beyond the People set may claim, which the members task settles.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 3 \\u00B7 b0ab0877]\\n\\n- I made nothing new. PR #77 is green on \\u0060b8cfee8\\u0060 (both build-test jobs in run 42214401578), which is the operator\\u0027s rebase of the branch onto main. That rebase is what fixed CI: the old failure was a \\u0060FlowRunRestartTests\\u0060 timeout from before PR #79\\u0027s flake fix, not a defect in this branch.\\n- If a later run sees red CI on this PR, check whether the branch still contains main\\u0027s flake fixes (\\u0060git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD\\u0060). Also check whether the jobs started at all, since a billing refusal shows up as jobs that never run. Only after that should you suspect the code.\\n- I left the branch untouched on purpose, because a green tree that matches what was tested needs no change.\\n\\n[Run 3 of 3 \\u00B7 696a25d6]\\n\\n- **What now exists:** the daemon stops every flow run on a parcel another node\\u0027s claim already wins at start-up, before advancing anything, whether or not the import loop is on (\\u0060LostClaims.YieldAllAsync\\u0060, called from \\u0060DaemonHost\\u0060). Applying a claim now also moves \\u0060Parcel.UpdatedAt\\u0060. Both changes are folded into their owning commits, and two fix replies are recorded for the platform to post after it pushes.\\n- **What to know:** the startup stop has to stay after the module feed positions are fixed. Otherwise the module never gets the stop and the worktree is left behind. A failure in one project is logged and the other projects are still checked.\\n- **Left undone:** I didn\\u0027t build each intermediate commit on its own, only the
